@copilot Update this PR directly with the module-local dispatcher design below. Do not create another PR, modify other PRs, merge anything, or change the draft state.

The user said: "I don't like encoding this information about specific test suites into here", referring to the workflow's suite-specific execution conditions, and "I want this to be simple". They also objected to adding a shared convention for this one module. They invoked /cloud to implement the following proposed simplification.

Replace the three suite-specific test-execution steps in .github/workflows/build-common.yml with one Test step making one Gradle invocation of :smoke-tests:smokeTest. Keep the existing matrix definitions and the separate compilation-only preparation step. The workflow should pass the suite name, the effective Linux-only reduced-selection flag, the generic OpenJ9 policy, and the existing cache option. Remove suite-specific execution branches such as checks for other/spring-aot and the WebSphere exception from this step. Suite interpretation and the existing vendor exceptions belong inside the smoke-test module, not YAML. Do not redesign the CI matrix.

Add smokeTest as a plain module-local Gradle lifecycle task with no actions. In smoke-tests/build.gradle.kts, choose its dependencies from the existing suite mapping: an explicit app-server suite in reduced mode selects testRepresentativeAppServers; full mode selects both testRepresentativeAppServers and testRemainingAppServers; non-app-server suites and the default combined suite select the existing test task. Keep test as a real Test task with its existing full/default behavior. Do not turn it into a fake lifecycle wrapper, clear its actions, invoke nested Gradle from an action, or mutate selection after task inputs are calculated.

Remove conventions/src/main/kotlin/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/gradle/SmokeTestSelection.kt from this PR. Keep the suite map and any small selection helper local to smoke-tests/build.gradle.kts instead of adding a shared plugin, shared convention, framework, or public build-logic API for one consumer. Adapt the associated convention tests so useful regression coverage remains without retaining a general production helper solely for those tests. Keep the Java annotation-based representative/remaining selection.

Preserve the accepted split-task behavior: main executes each effective app-server case once across two disjoint tasks, reduced Linux PRs use the identical representative task recipe that main populates, Windows PRs retain full supported coverage, and TomEE's Linux OpenJ9 representatives are not accidentally excluded by the generic skip policy. Keep empty partitions empty, full/default direct test invocations working, and other/spring-aot/none behavior intact. Retain all meaningful cache inputs including effective container platform and agent/extension/test-app/fixture artifacts. Non-app-server recipes must not vary with irrelevant app-server policy flags. Preserve anonymous read-only PR remote caching and trusted-upload/local-cache safeguards.

Retain or adapt focused regression coverage for dispatcher dependency selection, one invocation without duplicate case execution, platform/vendor cases, empty groups, and representative cache-input equality between PR and main. Apply narrow formatting immediately before behavioral validation. Validate actual selected tasks and inputs, not merely workflow syntax. If remote-cache access, Docker, or other environment limitations prevent a check, report the limitation rather than weakening assertions or claiming a cache hit.

Keep the change focused on simplifying this PR. Do not add changed-file detection, cache warmup steps, dependency-cache persistence, Muzzle changes, new configuration knobs, or unrelated cleanup.
